trial_court: Civil Judge, Senior Division, Nilanga (Regular Civil Suit No. 210 of 2004)
case_name: Govind S/O. Manohar Jadhav, Gopal S/O. ... vs Smt. Rukhminibai W/O. Manohar Jadhav

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Govind S/O. Manohar Jadhav, Gopal S/O. ... (sons of Manohar)
parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Rukhminibai W/O. Manohar Jadhav (wife of Manohar and mother of Govind and Gopal)

facts_of_case: Manohar married Rukminibai, then Popatbai. Appellants are sons of Manohar from Popatbai. Respondent Sundarabai purchased property from Rukminibai pending the suit. Trial court held that suit property excluding Survey No. 13 was ancestral property.

legal_principles.principle: Children of void marriages are deemed to be legitimate for the purpose of inheriting separate property.
legal_principles.held: Appellant No. 1 and 2 would be treated as legitimate sons of Manohar Jadhav for the purpose of inheriting separate property of Manohar Jadhav.

legal_principles.principle: Sons and daughters born out of void or voidable marriage are deemed to be children born in lawful wedlock.
legal_principles.held: He referred to definition of 'Separate Property' given in Section 228 of the Principles of Hindu Law (Volume I, 20th Edition), Sub-section 6 is to the effect that whenever there is partition and a coparcener obtains a share on partition and if he has no (legitimate) issue, the property allotted to him on partition will partake the nature of separate property.

outcome.final_order: Partition of remaining land between appellant No. 4 and respondent No. 1 only.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
